newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on caution before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on caution before FOMC.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell Monday in cautious trading ahead of the two-day meeting of the Federal Reserve, the U.S. central bank, which starts on Tuesday.
"The market was very dull, with everyone awaiting the outcome of the meeting," said Javier Lopez, a trader with the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC share index lost 10.67 points to 3,636.50. Volume was thin at 46.9 million shares traded.
Most economists believe policy-makers at the Fed will vote to hold interest rates steady at the meeting, which ends on Wednesday.
Analysts also said the market was in a seasonal lull prior to annual corporate earnings reports.

"We're in a waiting period while we revalue companies based on their earnings. What little buying there is is very selective," said Roberto Garcia, investment adviser at the Monterrey-based Vector brokerage.
"The trend is a little negative, as some macroeconomic data has not been as good as we were expecting, like inflation and retail sales," he said.
In the broader market, 100 stocks traded, with losers beating gainers 46 to 37.
Most heavily traded was Telmex, whose L shares fell eight centavos (one cent) to 14.70 pesos ($1.88), while its American Depository Receipts ended off 1/8 to 37-1/2.
Financial group Bancomer followed Telmex, off six centavos (one cent) to 2.80 pesos (36 cents). Traders noted the stock was downgraded by Bear Stearns.
Most active gainer was packaging company Empaq, up 12 centavos (two cents) to 4.92 pesos (63 cents). Dealers described the issue as an illiquid stock that had lagged the market.
